name: Andrew
title: Apostle and the First-Called Disciple
summary: Andrew was one of Jesus' first disciples and the brother of Simon Peter. He was from Bethsaida by the Sea of Galilee and worked as a fisherman. Originally, he was a disciple of John the Baptist, but followed Jesus after the Baptist's testimony about him as "the Lamb of God". In Eastern church tradition, he is called "the First-called" (Protokletos). Andrew is known for his role in bringing people to Jesus – first his brother Peter, later the boy with bread and fish at the feeding of the five thousand, and Greeks who wanted to meet Jesus. He is counted among the twelve apostles and was a witness to central events in Jesus' ministry.

keyEvents.title: Meeting with Jesus
keyEvents.description: Andrew was a disciple of John the Baptist and followed Jesus when the Baptist pointed him out as "the Lamb of God". He spent the day with Jesus and became the first to be called to follow him.

keyEvents.title: Peter Brought to Jesus
keyEvents.description: The first thing Andrew did was find his brother Simon and say: "We have found the Messiah!" and bring him to Jesus, who gave Simon the name Cephas (Peter).

keyEvents.title: The Call at the Sea of Galilee
keyEvents.description: Jesus called Andrew and Peter while they were casting nets into the sea, saying: "Follow me, and I will make you fish for people." They immediately left their nets and followed him.

keyEvents.title: The Boy with the Lunch
keyEvents.description: At the feeding of the five thousand, it was Andrew who found the boy with five barley loaves and two fish and brought him to Jesus, even though he wondered what that could be enough for.

keyEvents.title: The Greeks Who Sought Jesus
keyEvents.description: When some Greeks wanted to meet Jesus, they approached Philip, who went to Andrew. Together they brought the Greeks to Jesus, illustrating Andrew's role as a bridge-builder.

versions.title: Peter's Brother
versions.reason: [minor] The title 'Peter's brother' is correct but somewhat limiting. Andrew was one of the first called apostles and known as one who brought people to Jesus. A more descriptive title could include his role as an apostle.; [major] Andrew lived and worked primarily during Jesus' lifetime. Although he was also active in the early church, his biblical role is mainly connected to Jesus' life and ministry. 'Jesus' is more appropriate as the primary era.; [minor] Andrew was a fisherman by trade before being called. The role 'fisherman' could be added for completeness.; [major] Footnotes are missing. There are several interesting historical, linguistic, and theological details about Andrew that should be covered.

footnotes.text: The name Andrew (Greek: Ἀνδρέας, Andreas) means 'manly' or 'brave' and is of Greek origin. It is remarkable that a Jewish fisherman from Galilee bore a Greek name, reflecting the Hellenistic influence in the region.

According to early Christian tradition (including Eusebius of Caesarea), Andrew served as a missionary in Scythia (modern-day Ukraine and southern Russia) and Greece. He is regarded as the patron saint of Scotland, Russia, and Greece, among others.
In Eastern Orthodox tradition, Andrew is referred to as 'Protokletos' (Πρωτόκλητος), meaning 'the first-called,' because according to the Gospel of John he was the first disciple to follow Jesus.

Bethsaida, the hometown of Andrew and Peter (John 1:44), was located on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee. Archaeological excavations at et-Tell and el-Araj have uncovered remains of first-century fishing villages that may be the biblical Bethsaida.

In the rabbinic and Jewish context, Galilee was known as an area with strong contact with Greco-Roman culture. The fact that both Andrew and Philip bore Greek names, and that the Greeks approached them specifically (John 12:20-22), suggests they served as cultural bridge-builders.
